text.p: A whopping boost in sales and steady copper prices spurred rave reviews from analysts about Grupo Mexico's (GMexico) second quarter earnings .
The copper giant reported earnings per share for the quarter of 1.03 pesos, slightly below an average forecast of 1.06 pesos from four analysts surveyed by Reuters.
"Their report was below last year's, but very impressive," BBV-Probursa Mexico City analyst Jose Buendia said.

GMexico reported net profit of 1.320 billion pesos for the first half of the year, down from 1.927 billion pesos in the year-ago period. Operating profit was 1.895 billion pesos from 2.414 billion pesos in the first six months of 1996.
The company's sales rose 30 percent in dollar terms in the second quarter from the first three months of the year.
Santander's Sandra Morfin in Mexico City said the revenue levels "may not be sustainable," but said the outlook looks good for the company.

"I think the company is undervalued compared to other copper producers. An expansion in smelter and refining capacity should offset a medium-term decline in copper prices," she said. Santander has a buy rating on the company.
Analysts said the operating margin for the period was between 29 and 35 percent. Grupo Mexico did not elaborate on the basic earnings results required by the stock excange.
The copper giant should continue to impress in the third quarter, as analysts said any improvement will shine in comparison with last year's dismal third quarter.
"Copper prices shouldn't fall much more and we expect a recovery in the third quarter compared to the horrible report last year," Buendia said.
Valores Finamex analyst Chris Albi also said the rest of the year will show a lighter tax burden.
"They provisioned more taxes than expected, which is why the earnings per share was a bit lower. This means in the third and fourth quarter they don't have to pay so much," he said.

Analysts said they will continue to keep an eye on possible future sales of shares held by Asarco. The U.S. copper firm sold 20 million Series L shares of Grupo Mexico a month ago and has a remaining 60.9 million L shares to sell.
